mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover from the recent dip, weekday foot traffic should rebuild and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if retail stays weak even as commuting mobility rises.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both averaging above their t-1w levels for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in WORKPLACES below the recent low reduces daily trip chaining and lunch-time shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks. The effect is strongest when TRANSIT is also falling.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -40 for a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after a weekly WORKPLACES mean below -40, especially if TRANSIT is also below its prior week.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in GROCERY_PHARM signals more local errands and neighborhood circulation, which spills over into nearby retail visits and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next week. The signal fails if grocery mobility rises but retail does not.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher in the following week after GROCERY_PHARM increases relative to the prior weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility is elevated while RESIDENTIAL remains muted, discretionary outdoor activity substitutes into nearby commercial streets and supports higher retail mobility over the next four weeks. The effect disappears if park use falls back or residential time rises sharply.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 10 for two straight weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over 28 days after two consecutive weeks with PARKS above 10 and RESIDENTIAL not rising.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates looser movement constraints and should translate into higher retail visitation with a lag of one to two weeks. The hypothesis fails if commuting mobility improves but retail remains below the recent four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 points week-on-week after a prior decline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -35.4 at t-1w and -29.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after TRANSIT posts a rebound of more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, more time spent at home suppresses discretionary shopping trips and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if residential time remains high but retail recovers anyway.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above its current weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: A combined weakening in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS indicates fewer neighborhood errands and outings, which reduces incidental retail exposure and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks. The effect should not hold if either series rebounds quickly.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both decline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days after two consecutive weekly declines in both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, TRANSIT contractions transmit quickly into lower retail footfall because fewer riders reach shopping districts. The effect should appear within one week and be strongest when WORKPLACES are also weak.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 while WORKPLACES stays below -35
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -35.4 at t-1w and WORKPLACES was -45.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the following week when TRANSIT is below -30 and WORKPLACES is below -35.
